passage.passage_text:
Jake, a resilient young boy, gazed at his new surroundings with wonder and determination. Having recently moved to a new town, he eagerly explored his neighborhood, hoping to make friends with the local kids.

One day, Jake stumbled upon an abandoned park with a damaged playground. The rusty swings creaked in the wind and the slide was covered in a thick layer of grime. Despite its disrepair, Jake saw potential in the playground. He decided to repair it, believing it could be a great way to make friends.

That evening, Jake discussed his plan with his parents. "This is a big task, Jake," his father warned. His mother added, "And you'll need help." But Jake was adamant. "I can do it," he asserted. His resilience shone through his unwavering determination.

Over the next few days, Jake worked tirelessly. He managed to gather abundant resources from around town and even rallied a few helpers. Bit by bit, the playground transformed. The rusty swings now glowed with a fresh coat of paint, and the slide gleamed under the sun.

Word spread about the revamped playground, and soon, children flocked to see it. Their faces lit up at the sight of the once-abandoned playground, now a vibrant space filled with laughter and joy. Jake's efforts had paid off. Not only did he breathe new life into the playground, but he also made plenty of new friends in the process. His resourcefulness and resilience had turned a desolate park into a haven of happiness for children in his new town.

recall_scoring.general_instructions: For each sentence, award 2 points if student recalls BOTH the character and key detail, 1 point for either one, 0 points for neither. Allow paraphrasing.

student_action: Phase 1 - Reading: Student reads the passage silently or aloud (as appropriate) from beginning to end. Student may take as much time as needed to read and understand the passage. Phase 2 - Recall: After reading, passage is removed/covered. Student orally recalls everything they remember from the passage. Student may include characters, events, details, and main ideas. Assessor records recalled sentences. Phase 3 - Questions: Passage is made visible again. Student answers multiple-choice comprehension questions (typically 5-6 questions). Student may refer back to the passage while answering questions. Student selects answer choice (A, B, or C).
assessor_grading: Assessor scores in three phases: Phase 1 - Reading: Observe and note reading behaviors, fluency, and any difficulties (not formally scored but noted). Phase 2 - Recall: For each sentence in the passage, assessor marks if student recalled: (1) the character/subject mentioned in sentence, (2) the key detail/action in sentence. Each sentence receives 2 points (both recalled), 1 point (one recalled), or 0 points (neither recalled). Total recall score = sum of sentence scores. Recall accuracy ratio = total points / max possible points. Phase 3 - Questions: Assessor marks each multiple-choice question as CORRECT (correct answer selected) or INCORRECT (wrong answer, multiple selections, or no response). Question score = total correct out of total questions. Overall comprehension performance combines both recall accuracy and question accuracy.

assessor_script: SETUP: Prepare assessment materials. Ensure student has access to passage and questions.
SAY TO STUDENT: 'I'm going to ask you to read this passage and then answer some questions about it. You can refer back to the passage while answering questions.'
• Allow student to read passage at their own pace
• Present questions one at a time
• Mark each answer as correct or incorrect
interface_spec.student_prompt: Read this passage and answer the questions that follow.
interface_spec.student_action: Student reads passage and answers questions. Student can refer back to passage while answering.
interface_spec.assessor_grading: Assessor marks each question as correct or incorrect. Calculate total score based on questions answered correctly.
